chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, who said:

I wrote to him asking him about a man who was single (sarur) and had never performed Hajj, who performed Hajj on behalf of another single man who had never performed Hajj. Does that one Hajj suffice for each of them for the Hajj of Islam, or not? Make that clear to me, O my master, if God wills. He wrote back: That does not suffice.

Therefore, the meaning in this report is that we should interpret it as: if the single man has wealth, then that one Hajj does not suffice for him. And we have narrated it in detail in the report of Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf. It is also possible that his saying 'That does not suffice' means for the one who performs Hajj when he becomes wealthy, because whoever performs Hajj on behalf of another and then becomes wealthy, Hajj becomes obligatory upon him. This indicates that.

key_terms.صَرُورَةٍ: A single man who has never been married

ai.seo_question: Does one Hajj suffice for two single men who have never performed Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahani, the Imam clarifies that a single man (sarur) performing Hajj on behalf of another single man does not discharge the obligatory Hajj for both parties. The commentary by Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates that this ruling hinges on the performer's financial capacity; if he possesses the means, the single Hajj is insufficient for his own obligation, and if he becomes wealthy after performing, the duty remains incumbent upon him.
